scope: official past-question boards permitted for the `official` provenance track

sa-nsc.copyrightBasis: South African Copyright Act 98 of 1978 — state works vest copyright in the state; term 50 years from first publication
sa-nsc.notes: DBE publishes NSC papers + marking memos openly for exam-prep use. Open publication != republication licence: verbal attribution alone does not clear copyright. Best practice: written permission from DBE before hosting verbatim papers; link-first where possible.
sa-nsc.attestationText: Source: National Senior Certificate past papers, Department of Basic Education, South Africa (education.gov.za). Used with attribution for educational exam preparation.

tz-necta.copyrightBasis: Tanzania Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act, 1999 (Act No. 7) — government works protected; term 50 years from publication
tz-necta.notes: NECTA publishes past papers openly on necta.go.tz / onlinesys.necta.go.tz. Same caveat as SA: open access is not a republication licence; request written permission from NECTA before verbatim hosting.
tz-necta.attestationText: Source: NECTA past papers, National Examinations Council of Tanzania (necta.go.tz). Used with attribution for educational exam preparation.

excludedFromOfficialTrack.reason: Past questions sold commercially by JAMB; not openly published; verbatim use requires licence
WAEC sells official past-question packs; asserts copyright; NECO papers not officially published openly

excludedFromOfficialTrack.board: IB / Cambridge International / College Board AP / SEAB
excludedFromOfficialTrack.reason: Commercial exam boards with active copyright enforcement; past papers sold or restricted-access

legalPrinciples: Exam questions are literary works protected by copyright in virtually all jurisdictions.
Free/open availability on a board website != licence to republish; always check terms of use.
Attribution is not permission — it does not cure infringement unless paired with an open licence (e.g. CC, open-government licence).
Facts, syllabus topics, and learning outcomes are not copyrightable: original JAMB-style / WAEC-style generation is safe as long as questions are not copied or adapted verbatim from actual papers.
Adapting a real past question = derivative work — same clearance required as verbatim copy.
